notes:
How it works:
- Perception: the head camera colour image is segmented by chromaticity (r/g/b share of brightness) for each cube colour. The largest connected blob is back-projected to world points using depth, pos and mat. The cube centre comes from the top-face points (the highest few mm) by fitting the smallest square around them; that fit also gives the yaw (mod 90°). Estimates are taken from two frames at the start.
- Grasp: top-down with the palm facing down. Candidate hand headings are the cube yaw + k·90°, kept within [-100°, 100°]. For each candidate I check: the 2D clearance of the finger and thumb footprint from the other cubes and the bin walls; IK reachability; self- and environment collisions, found with mj_collision on the private model with the hand in its pre-curl pose (hand–table touches are ignored). If the flat palm doesn't work, palm tilts of ±0.3/±0.5 rad are tried. For each candidate the planner warm-starts IK along the whole straight-line path (pre-grasp 6.5 cm above the cube → grasp → vertical lift) and checks every point, then plays the chain back as joint targets with smooth timing. The fingers are pre-curled (closure 0.3) before descending, so the final finger sweep is small. Closure then ramps to 1.
- Recovery: (a) if the hand stops more than 6 mm above the grasp height (it hit a neighbouring cube or obstacle), it backs off and replans with that heading penalised. (b) After lifting, the head camera checks the cube. If it is still on the table, the controller regrasps at the new position. If it is held more than 3.2 cm off-centre, the controller puts it down, goes home, looks again and regrasps (up to 3 attempts in total).
- Place: a straight-line path, also checked with IK and collisions, from the lift point to 15 cm above the bin centre while the hand turns smoothly to the best place heading. Then it lowers to a cube-centre height of 0.865, opens the hand and retreats upward.

Results: on the practice runs it succeeded about 88–92% of the time (36/40 and 22/26 on unseen batches, 33/36 on a set that included 7 known-hard seeds).

Known weaknesses:
- Crowded layouts near the robot's centreline (y ≈ -0.1 to -0.2) are the main failure. Reach there is limited by the arm hitting the torso, the only reachable grasps can be tilted ones, and a neighbouring cube can get pushed or knocked off the table (one "dropped" outcome).
- Repeated regrasps can still run past the 25 s limit.
- Checking the cube while it is held is affected by the hand blocking the camera's view (about 1–2 cm bias). If the cube can't be seen, the grasp is assumed to be fine.
- Planning steps take up to a few seconds of wall-clock time in the worst case.
- Not tested under different lighting, camera noise or calibration error. The colour thresholds are based on brightness ratios, which should make them fairly tolerant of lighting changes.
